entities.summary:
Nebmaatre represents one of the most enigmatic pharaohs of the late Second Intermediate Period, a tumultuous epoch in Ancient Egyptian history spanning approximately 1650 to 1550 BCE. His prenomen, 'Lord of Justice is Re,' is attested primarily on a single scarab seal, suggesting a short or regionally confined reign. Scholars like Jürgen von Beckerath propose he belonged to the 16th Dynasty, ruling from Thebes over a fractured Upper Egypt, while others speculate a connection to the early 17th Dynasty, which eventually expelled the Hyksos and reunited Egypt. His existence underscores the decentralized nature of power during this period, marked by the concurrent rule of the Hyksos 15th Dynasty in the North and various local Egyptian dynasties in the South.

The scarcity of archaeological evidence surrounding Nebmaatre means no significant achievements or specific events can be attributed directly to his rule. Unlike more prominent pharaohs, no grand monuments, extensive building projects, or military campaigns are recorded under his name. His perceived authority would likely have been limited to the Theban nome and possibly its immediate surroundings, navigating a complex political landscape where tribute might have been paid to the Hyksos or alliances formed with other southern principalities. His appearance in king lists, if at all, would have been fleeting, a testament to the ephemeral nature of many rulers during a time of internal strife and foreign occupation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nebmaatre's historical importance lies in representing the fragmented political landscape of the Second Intermediate Period and the resilience of native Egyptian rule in Upper Egypt. His obscure reign, though lacking major events, contributes to our understanding of the transitional phase leading to the reunification of Egypt under the New Kingdom.
